# Appeal of Denial – Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04, Reference Number POC-DF42BEB029-97975**
**Member: Quinn Ellison, Member ID: W391580594**
**Plan: Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Montana**
**Governing Policy: Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty, https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html**

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the plan's own coverage criteria, applied to my medical records, support that conclusion.

## Why I believe the denial should be reconsidered

The denial states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that the plan review the following points against its own policy.

**1. My imaging shows single-compartment disease, which is what the plan's policy for this procedure addresses.**

The plan's policy states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My MRI from 2026-05-28 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. The records do not describe involvement of the lateral or patellofemoral compartments. This is the single-compartment pattern the policy describes as appropriate for a partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, not a total knee replacement.

The policy also states:

> "Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria (see also Additional Note):"

My MRI findings of advanced (bone-on-bone, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) osteoarthritis limited to the medial compartment fit this description. [Please confirm with the surgeon's office that the specific device planned for use is FDA-approved, if this detail is needed for the file.]

**2. My records document the conservative therapy the plan's policy calls for.**

The policy states:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My records show 16 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (24 visits, from 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17), documented in the physical therapy discharge note, along with 8 months of NSAID use and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-02 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This exceeds the 12-week minimum described in the policy, and the physical therapy portion was formal, in-person, and licensed as the policy requires.

**3. My records support why further conservative care would not be expected to help.**

The policy states:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral) or severe angular deformity, or for avascular necrosis with collapse of tibial or femoral condyle, or progressive flexion contracture."

My MRI documents bone-on-bone articulation in the medial (weight-bearing) compartment. Despite this, I completed 16 weeks of physical therapy, 8 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection, and I continue to have pain that wakes me 3-4 times nightly and limits my ability to climb stairs without assistance. My exam findings include positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side.

I have already completed the treatment the plan's own policy asks for, and my imaging shows the specific pattern of disease the policy identifies as appropriate for this procedure. I am asking the plan to explain, in light of its own stated criteria above, how the imaging in my file falls short, or to reverse the denial.

## What I am requesting

I am requesting that Aetna reconsider and reverse this denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) recommended by Dr. Lindqvist. If any additional records or clarification would help resolve this appeal, please let me or my surgeon's office know what is needed.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-31. I am submitting it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and/or by fax to 859-425-3379. I have also confirmed [insert mailing address from denial letter, if different] as the address for this appeal, and I may follow up by phone at 1-800-872-3862 if needed.

Thank you for reviewing my appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Quinn Ellison
Member ID: W391580594
Date: [insert date of signing]
Contact phone: [insert phone number]
Contact address: [insert mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
